description: Decomposes the ~1e-8 Schur-Weyl self-check residual of the rho_k_h3a probes into q_0 pin straddle (98%), witness internal self-inconsistency (2%), and the identity itself (0%; 3.1e-49 at the 50-dps floor). Refutes bean qdzu's precision-floor hypothesis and localises the residual entirely in input provenance.
caveats: DEFECT RECORDED, and it is a CALIBRATION-LAYER crossing plus a witness-internal inconsistency -- NOT the numeric-engine precision floor that bean qdzu hypothesised. The rho_k_h3a probes evaluate Sum_lambda y_lambda chi^lambda at the EXPERIMENTAL (proton) q_0 from q_parameter.Q_MP while reading tr_M from atomic-tr-m-mpfr-50dps.witness.json, which is stamped q0Anchor='muon' (the IDEAL 3-CAL layer). The 11.5371 ppb separation is the mu-p substrate tension itself and accounts for 98% of the reported ~8.5e-8. The remaining 2% (1.852e-9) is the witness disagreeing with ITSELF: its results.tr_M_at_q0_50dps and its results.peel_cross_check.tr_M_at_q0_50dps differ by that amount, and the independently-computed Schur-Weyl sum matches the PEEL branch to 3.1e-49 while missing the PRIMARY branch by 1.852e-9 -- evidence that the primary value, not the identity, is the wrong number. With the pin matched and the peel branch used, the residual is 3.1e-49, i.e. the actual 50-dps engine floor. The identity itself was already proved to hold identically in q at n=3 and n=6 (PR #5168, bean qou-hdyp); beta_D on H_6 with 23 crossings is that proof's n=6 atom. Correct layer for this probe is MUON, matching its input witness -- moving only the evaluation pin to proton would invert the straddle rather than remove it, and regenerating the input witness at proton is gated behind bean qou-1c4y.
